channel.title: MIND / MATTER Daily Briefing
channel.description: New research across consciousness, quantum foundations, and neuroscience.

item.title: Tunable spectral correlations of highly multimode visible light via broadband quantum frequency conversion
item.description: Multimode squeezed states of light are a resource for achieving quantum advantage in computing and sensing, where spatial or temporal modes have been the experimental norm. In our experiments, we generated highly frequency-multimode infrared quantum light and showed how adiabatic frequency conversion can be used to convert the quantum state to visible wavelengths while concurrently manipulating the joint spectrum by realizing a configurable many-port frequency-domain beamsplitter unitary transformation.

item.title: A Transdisciplinary Science of Information within the Organogram of Consciousness
item.description: Information transcends the traditional disciplines of physics, psychology, cosmology, and biology, yet remains connected to them through Zero-Point Energy. Although the origins of space, time, and matter are known, the when and how of Information’s emergence remain elusive.

item.title: Multimodal Coma Stimulation to Improve Arousal and Physical Function in Patients with Traumatic Brain Injury
item.description: Background: Impaired consciousness is one of the most serious complications following Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI). Sensory deprivation may delay neural recovery and worsen patient outcomes.

item.title: Quantum tomography of fermion pairs in e + e − collisions: Longitudinal beam polarization effects
item.description: We present a quantum tomography study of fermion pair production at future e + e − colliders, emphasizing how longitudinal beam polarization controls the two-qubit spin density matrix. We study the processes e + e − → t t ‾ , e + e − → μ + μ − and Bhabha scattering e + e − → e + e − , representing the mass threshold behavior, the Z pole resonance and the s / t -channel interplay.

item.title: Nambu’s Dynamics, Strings, and Gravitized Quantum Theory
item.description: In this article, we present a new view on string theory that is rooted in quantum foundations extended to the domain of quantum gravity in the form of gravitized quantum theory, in which the canonical probability measure captured by the Born rule of quantum theory, turns out to be dynamical and contextual. We claim that this gravitization of quantum theory is the essence of string theory.

item.title: Body in memory: the role of bodily self-consciousness in episodic memory and autonoetic consciousness
item.description: Episodic memory (EM) enables the conscious recollection of personally experienced events, including contextual features such as visual, auditory and emotional details. However, the role of bodily signals has been largely neglected in EM, although the observer's body provides a rich bodily context during the encoding, storage and recall of events, and has recently been associated with a bodily form of self-consciousness (bodily self-consciousness; BSC).

item.title: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
item.description: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit.

item.title: Soft Mixture of Quantum Experts for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Learning
item.description: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has attracted increasing interest as a possible route to construct feature representations that are difficult to reproduce with classical models. However, near-term QML architectures based on trainable parametrized quantum circuits remain affected by limited hardware resources, noise, and severe optimization difficulties such as barren plateaus.

item.title: A provably efficient classical algorithm for simulating OTOC$^{(1)}$ in 1D
item.description: Out-of-time-order correlators (OTOCs) are quantities of broad interest in many-body physics due to their connection with information scrambling and quantum chaos. Recently, estimating higher-order OTOCs in random quantum circuits was proposed as a promising avenue for quantum advantage, yet the classical hardness of this task remains poorly understood.

item.title: Spontaneous emission of atomic systems near metallic and semiconducting atomic chains
item.description: We investigate the spontaneous emission of a quantum emitter placed near finite atomic chains described by the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. By tuning the chain from a metallic to a semiconducting character through dimerization, we analyze how the electronic structure of an atomic-scale scatterer, together with the illumination profile, determines the strength, bandwidth, and spatial structure of the spontaneous emission enhancement.

item.title: Gradient Blindness in Adaptive Architecture Search for IQP Born Machines
item.description: Instantaneous quantum polynomial (IQP) Born machines learn a probability distribution from data with a circuit of commuting gates that a classical computer trains at hundreds of qubits. Adaptive algorithms grow a sparse circuit from a small seed by adding in every round the candidate gates with the largest loss gradient.

item.title: Quantum Annealing with a Quantum Neural Network: Width of Annealing Matters
item.description: Quantum annealing is a promising quantum algorithm for dealing with computationally hard optimization problems. Currently available hardware can implement the algorithm for a significant class of Hamiltonian problems.

item.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
item.description: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. While they differ in their theoretical commitments, both aim to advance neuroscientific investigations of consciousness without succumbing to the intelligibility problem: the impossibility for scientific inquiries to provide intelligible access to subjective experience.

item.title: 100 ± Δ t years of quantum uncertainty: From origins to modern insights
item.description: Heisenberg’s uncertainty principle is a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, marking a decisive departure from classical physics. Conceived almost a century ago through a thought experiment showing that measuring an electron’s position inevitably disturbs its momentum, it began as a deceptively simple idea that sparked countless studies and grew into the rich research field it is today.
